artefacts.description: Scope, goals, constraints, stakeholders and how success will be judged.
artefacts.name: Project charter

phases.name: Setup
phases.summary: Agree what is being built, for whom, and how the project will run.

artefacts.description: Who will use the product and what each of them needs.
artefacts.name: Personas

artefacts.description: The problem being solved, in the users' words, and why it matters.
artefacts.name: Problem statement

artefacts.description: Where the product is heading and the measurable objectives that say it got there.
artefacts.name: Vision and objectives

artefacts.description: What the product must do, one numbered requirement at a time.
artefacts.name: Functional requirements

artefacts.description: Performance, security, availability and the other qualities the product must have.
artefacts.name: Non-functional requirements

artefacts.description: Requirements grouped into epics and features that can be planned and built.
artefacts.name: Epics and features

phases.name: Requirements
phases.summary: Capture who the product is for and what it must do.

artefacts.description: How each persona moves through the product to get something done.
artefacts.name: User journey

artefacts.description: Rough layouts of each screen, to agree structure before visual design.
artefacts.name: Low-fidelity wireframes

artefacts.description: Detailed, styled screens ready for the front-end build.
artefacts.name: High-fidelity wireframes

phases.name: Design
phases.summary: Work out how people will use the product, before deciding how it is built.

artefacts.description: The main parts of the system and what each one is responsible for.
artefacts.name: Component overview

artefacts.description: How the parts fit together, with data, interfaces, technology choices and key decisions.
artefacts.name: High-level design

artefacts.description: Endpoints, tables and rules detailed enough to build from.
artefacts.name: Low-level design

artefacts.description: A diagram of how a request and its data move through the system.
artefacts.name: Flow diagram

artefacts.description: A diagram of who does what with the system.
artefacts.name: Use-case diagram

phases.name: Architecture
phases.summary: Decide the parts of the system, how they fit together, and the detail needed to build them.

artefacts.description: One set of Markdown instruction files for a coding tool - a foundation file, one file for each use case, and the acceptance tests - each pointing at the design items it builds.
artefacts.name: Build instructions

phases.name: Build & Test
phases.summary: Write the instruction files a person gives to a coding tool (Copilot, Claude, GPT or Gemini) so that tool builds the application. This system does not write the application.

artefacts.description: Where it runs, in what order things happen, and how to go back if it goes wrong.
artefacts.name: Deployment plan

artefacts.description: What is in this release, in words the business can read.
artefacts.name: Release notes

by_hand.description: Checks a person works through by hand, with a go or no-go for each. No model is used.
by_hand.name: Deployment verification

phases.name: Deploy

not_enabled.name: Infrastructure as code
not_enabled.reason: Not enabled. The product is built and run outside this tool, so there is nothing for it to describe yet. It can be switched on later.

not_enabled.name: CI/CD pipeline
not_enabled.reason: Not enabled. No automated build or release is wanted yet. It can be switched on later.

phases.summary: Plan the release, say what is in it, and check by hand that it worked.

artefacts.description: Step-by-step instructions for operating and recovering the product.
artefacts.name: Runbook

artefacts.description: Extra support in the first weeks after go-live, and when it ends.
artefacts.name: Hypercare plan

by_hand.description: Statements a named person accepts or does not accept, one by one, to record that support takes the product. No model is used.
by_hand.name: Handover sign-off

phases.name: BAU handover

not_enabled.name: Support guide
not_enabled.reason: Not enabled. Not needed yet; the runbook covers day-to-day problems. It can be switched on later.

not_enabled.name: SLOs and alerts
not_enabled.reason: Not enabled. No alerting is set up for a product built and run outside this tool. It can be switched on later.

not_enabled.name: Knowledge-transfer pack
not_enabled.reason: Not enabled. Not needed yet; the runbook and the sign-off cover what support must know. It can be switched on later.

phases.summary: Hand the running product to the people who will support it day to day, and record that they accept it.
